prerequisites: practical knowledge of programming languages explained in "Programming Methodology"
ability to read and understand documentation written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety, or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical, and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and to describe, analyze, evaluate, and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge to problem-solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Understand computer architecture and identify and evaluate the performance and scalability of computer systems used for processing large volumes of data.
Know and understand the concept of a distributed system.
Understand communication between services and their aggregation.
Understand the different architectural models of distributed systems and select the most appropriate for a given problem.
Design and deploy distributed systems using cloud services.
Know and apply techniques to increase reliability, availability, and performance in distributed systems.

syllabus_topics: Communication between services at the socket level
Consumption and development of APIs over HTTP

assessment_methods.method: Deliverables and defenses (two submissions/tests for laboratory work)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a final grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 is required. A minimum of 4.5 out of 10 must be obtained in the average of theoretical controls and in the average of practical deliveries. A minimum attendance of 70% to practical sessions (resulting in a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 for assistance) is also required. If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.45 * TEO + 0.4 * PRAC + 0.05 * ASIST + 0.1 * CV; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, students take a theoretical exam (ET) and a practical exam (EP), each requiring a minimum of 4.5. The final grade is 0.50 * ET + 0.50 * EP; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. Students granted differentiated evaluation will be assessed based on a theoretical exam (50%) and a practical exam (50%).
